nodes.text: 1. Form 3 of Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers-Disclosure scheme will be enabled shortly

2. Due dates for filing of Income Tax Returns and Audit Reports for AY 2026-27 are extended in the cases of persons mentioned at Sl.No.2 in the Table below Explanation2 to Sub-section (1) of Section 139 of Income Tax Act 1961 vide Circular No.07/2026 dated 28th September,2026.
3. Form 1 under the “Foreign Assets of Small Taxpayers Disclosure Scheme” is now available for filing.
4. ITR-1, ITR-2, ITR-3, ITR-4, ITR-5, ITR-6 and ITR-7 for AY 2026-27 are available for filing through both online and offline utilities.
5. Filing of TDS/TCS Correction Statements pertaining to Tax Year 2026-27 has been enabled.

6. Demand Management Facilitation Centre (DFC), has been set up to guide Taxpayers on issues/grievances regarding their outstanding demands. DFC may be contacted through the e-mail id: taxdemand@cpc.incometax.gov.in or on the toll-free number - 1800 309 0131 or chargeable no. 0821-6671200.
7. Excel utilities for filing Updated return for ITR-1 to 7 for AY 2022-23 as per Finance Act, 2026 are available for filing !

GST-registered businesses are required to file applicable returns or statements with the tax authorities. GST returns generally contain details of . Timely and accurate filing helps businesses maintain compliance and claim eligible ITC.
outward supplies, tax liability, and eligible input tax credit
The applicable GST form depends on the taxpayer’s registration type and activities. Key forms include:
– Reports details of outward supplies of goods and services by regular taxpayers.
– Summary return used by applicable taxpayers to declare tax liability and claim eligible input tax credit.
– Annual return applicable to taxpayers under the composition scheme, subject to applicable rules.
– Return for persons required to deduct TDS under GST.
– Statement filed by e-commerce operators required to collect TCS.
– Final return after cancellation or surrender of GST registration.
– Statement for persons holding a Unique Identity Number (UIN) seeking refunds.
is an auto-drafted statement of inward supplies, rather than a return that the taxpayer files.
– Access the official GST portal and log in with your credentials.
– Choose the relevant return and filing period.
– Report outward supplies, tax liability, and eligible ITC as applicable.
– Match return data with invoices, books, and available GST records.
– Pay any balance tax liability after adjusting eligible credits.
– Verify and file the return using the applicable authentication method, such as DSC or EVC.
– Keep the filed return and ARN for future reference.
